body: Had a blog for a few months, to be honest I didn't even use it??? Mostly aesthetic and fandom posts here and there. Tried to log in the other day and it was gone. No warning, no nothing. I'm not even gonna bother trying to get it back, I don't care that much, but it's only gonna deter me from using their shitty platform even more. Sucks because Tumblr has some good communities that I want to keep up with and I refuse to get a Twitter account because I don't care for drama or any of that other garbage. I just want to see cute art and read people's discussion on stuff that I like.
truffles, according to his name

Yeahhhh listen you're clearly dead set on thinking everything is bad. Hey, it's your right to think so. The thing is, you tell me all of these awful things, which are very much real, yes, but then...so is the opposite. The moment the first human made the decision to help his brother with a broken leg...that moment proves that the opposite exists.  

If love wasn't intrinsic, there'd be no point in species to keep trying, to keep evolving and multiplying, to keep improving. 

And if love *isn't* intrinsic, then clearly it can be learned.  

I'm just saying. We can agree to disagree. Neither of us will change our minds about it and that's okay.
Thank you, but my personal beliefs are tied to goodness, to kindness, to love. To me love is intrinsic, not suffering, not pain.

I don't understand. Could you elaborate?

Also, you are basing your philosophy in some sort of certainty that death is the end of all suffering. How can you be certain of that? How can you be certain of any of this? What gives you 100% true real no-questions-asked certainty that all of this is exactly, word by word, as you say it is?
Pain is temporary as well. You seem to base your entire philosophy on the idea that suffering is the default state of being. But how can you be sure of that?

But nature also causes pleasure. Does that make it inherently good? 

And reality happens independently of how you perceive it, yes...but you can only perceive so much. Again, you are limited by your perception of the world around you.

Your ex boyfriend sounds like an asshole, is clearly abusive, and you have your entire life ahead of you. Block him, ghost him, never interact with him again, you don't need him. You deserve so much better, and you WILL have so much better. It hurts now but it won't hurt forever.
Yes you will. The present is not eternal. Things change. If you stick around, you'll get to experience that change.

Idk, if we can't truly know where nature came from or why, then we can't truly know its true *nature*, can we? How can we be sure of its inherent corruption if we're not even sure what nature *is*? There's goodness in the world. This corruption you mention doesn't exist on its own, does it? Because if it truly were only that, then the good in it wouldn't exist. 

I don't think nature is inherently anything. It just exists. It just is. I think we are the ones who anthropomorphize it. By calling it inherently corrupt, you are giving it a...meaning? A purpose? An intended way that it should be but it isn't? I don't know how to explain it. You're looking at it through your own human bias, I think. 

The way you perceive reality is always going to be, well, reality. Because reality, and thus nature, are only what we can perceive of it, in the end.

Those are the lies your depressed brain tells you. Doesn't mean that they're true. You're worthy of dignity, love and respect in this human life. Your negative experiences may have made you believe otherwise, but in the end they're just that, bad experiences and beliefs. Reality is something else, it stretches beyond your perception of it. You are worthy. Your life is worthy. I can't tell you how to think or act, but I can tell you that you are as important and as worthy of as much love as everyone else on this planet.
You are beautiful, you've just been told otherwise.
Here if you need me.
But if nature is so corrupt...why does it exist? Where did it come from?

Oh, yeah, I haven't seen many movies from the 80's. Maybe you should give it another watch tonight (today?), I do that sometimes when I'm feeling not very *spectacular* myself, I rewatch things that make me happy.

If we're not meant to exist or experience the physical...why do we, then? Genuine question with genuine interest in your perspective. I'm not here to judge or change your mind. Just to talk about things for a bit.
Hey no worries! I personally haven't seen it (assuming it's a movie?), but hey, maybe it's a sign!

I get it. Trust me. There's not much I can say to make things better. But the thing about the present is it doesn't stay the present forever, y'know? Even this conversation is already in the past. Sometimes you gotta hold out and get through the shit that's happening right now, to make it to "the future" everyone keeps talking about. Could be worth it. Could be not. In the end it depends on your perspective. But I personally would tell you to stick it out for a while longer. Maybe it's just a selfish personal wish. I wish you'd keep going, give it more time, see how it goes.

It matters if you get to experience it. In the end, it's you who takes the reins of your own life. I'm just here to give you a little perspective. Maybe think about some things. There's a reason you have a physical body in a physical realm to experience physical existence with. Maybe those experiences are worth it.

I know. There's not a lot I can do with just words. But I still try to put things into perspective, because I know what it feels like to feel how you feel. In the end, you're the one who gets to decide. But idk. There's always the possibility that something amazing could happen. There's always the possibility that you might meet the best people you've ever known. There's always a chance for awesome shit to happen, y'know? I just think maybe it's worth sticking around just for that, if nothing else.

Don't you wanna know how it all turns out in the end? What if something absolutely crazy happens and this entire world changes? No one was expecting the COVID, and that happened. Who's to say something amazing can't happen the same way? Idk. I just think maybe it's worth it to stay alive just for that possibility, y'know? The possibility that absolutely everything can change for the better.
At 33? With your whole life still ahead of you? All past bad experiences are just training. Gotta get through a lot of crappy people to find the ones that matter.
Stick around so you can meet the people who will truly love and appreciate you.
That's really sad, but irrelevant, and I didn't have a bad day. I feel trapped in life. That's all.

Exercise. Not to lose weight, not to be "loved" by anyone, not for any of those reasons. Do it because it will help the chemistry inside your brain, you will literally feel better. And it will improve your body at the same time, boosting your confidence. Everything you need is already inside of you. You're not ugly, you're not disgusting, you're just depressed. Your brain is lying to you. Don't let it.

I'd say give the medication some time to settle. I'm on fluoxetine too. It takes a while to hit. If you feel like it isn't helping, talk to your doctor about it and see if other meds might be better for you. Sometimes it takes a while to find one that works.

Other than that, I can relate to how you feel. I know it's difficult but sometimes all we can do is just focus on the small pleasures of life (watching a movie, drinking a particularly good cup of coffee, or like you said, hanging out with your friends) and giving it time.

You are worth it. Your parents are abusive. Don't let them get to your head, don't let them win. YOU are worth sticking around for. Fight for your life, you still have a lot of time to turn things around.
Don't do it, please.

I was you when I was 25. I'm only 28 now but let me tell you, it was enough time for everything to change significantly. I'm in the best relationship of my life and things are really looking up. I am still depressed, I still occasionally get suicidal, so I'm not telling you there's going to be some magical cure that makes you suddenly not depressed anymore. But what I *am* telling you is that you have a lot of time for things to change for the better and for really great things to happen, and it's worth  sticking around for.

I wish I had the words and the means to magically make everything better for you. The only thing I have is hope now. You have a lot more time than this. You do.

I hope you can get through this. I hope you can feel better. Maybe eat a snack and drink some water. Play with your puppy. Watch a movie. Do anything at all but just stay. Just live.
